Routines for spare blankets on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page teaches why
Spare blankets matter because they keep the cabin setup calm, clean, and ready for an animal that needs a softer landing after check-in. On a busy shift, you should treat each blanket as part of the pet's comfort kit, not as extra fabric to toss around. Keep them folded neatly, handle them with clean hands, and move them only when the bag is open and the pet area has been verified.

When a traveler arrives with a rabbit, stay steady and use the same warm, professional tone you would offer to any family. <<FACT F064>> If the crate looks crowded or the customer seems unsure, pause the handoff and get the senior coordinator involved before you continue. Always check the health paperwork at the same point, because missing or stale documents slow the whole desk and create avoidable stress. <<FACT F082>> Never guess, never rush past a detail, and never let a paper concern become a cabin problem.

For spare blankets, watch for dampness, strong odor, loose threads, or anything that could snag on a carrier latch. If a blanket is used, separate it from the clean stack right away and send it to the proper laundry bin. If you are short on clean stock, tell the shift lead early so the next traveler does not face a delay. The goal is simple: each animal gets patient attention, each customer gets clear guidance, and Aurelia Skyways keeps the Companion Animal Travel Desk dependable from the first greeting to the final handoff.

Remember to stay calm, check each item, and protect comfort and paperwork every time.
